title: Vein doctor visit (phlebologist)
what: The vein doctor examines your legs and usually does a vein ultrasound right away. This shows the condition of your veins and whether you need treatment.
why: For spider veins, bulging veins, swelling and heavy legs, night cramps, or after a blood clot.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes including the vein ultrasound; result right away
tell_doctor: When the veins, swelling or heaviness began
Whether you or your relatives have had blood clots
Whether you take hormones or blood thinners
Pregnancy now or plans for pregnancy

prepare.title: Legs
prepare.text: Do not put cream on your legs on the day of the visit. No need to shave.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that are easy to take off below the waist.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Swelling shows better in the afternoon. Ask the clinic what time is best.

bring: Compression stockings, if you wear them
steps: The doctor asks about your complaints
Examines your legs while you stand
Does a vein ultrasound by moving a probe with gel over your leg
Sometimes asks you to tense up or cough during the scan
Suggests treatment: stockings, medicines or procedures
feel: The exam and ultrasound do not hurt
after: If you were given stockings, wear them as the doctor said
Walk more and do not sit for long without moving
Come back for a follow-up when the doctor says
red_flags: A leg suddenly swells, hurts and turns red: see a doctor urgently
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call your local emergency number

faq.q: Are spider veins on the legs dangerous?
faq.a: Most often they are a cosmetic issue. But it is worth having your veins checked.

faq.q: Do varicose veins always need surgery?
faq.a: Not always. There are small procedures and non-surgical treatment. The doctor decides.

reminders.text: Vein doctor visit tomorrow. Do not put cream on your legs, and bring your past vein ultrasounds.
